row.name: OpenBind-0
row.note: OpenBind-0 is the OpenFold3 stack on upstream's v0.5.0 checkpoint. It folds this page's fixture at the same three recycles and 200 sampling steps as the OpenFold3 row, resolved by the same code path, so the two rows are directly comparable. It also takes ligands, which OpenFold3 refuses. Its own GPU reference exists but not on this fixture: on a single-sequence 512-residue apo target an H200 takes 9.311 s of device time (perf/openbind/gpu_reference.json, cell ob_apo_512_s1) against 36.017 s on one Blackhole AI Processor, the latter measured on this host during the port and not committed to this repo. This page's fixture carries a 35-sequence alignment and MSA depth is a trunk cost, so that pair is context, not a cell. The reference also records its own 512-residue rung moving 10.65 % between two independently rented H200s, because the 200-step rollout is launch-bound and carries the landlord's CPU.

p150a.parity: Release-gate floor, 3.5 A CA RMSD and 0.70 TM (scripts/release_gate.py), fixed before this number existed and measured at 1.693 A / 0.894 on 7ROA. That is the gate's floor for the model, not a per-fixture check on this target, which has no experimental structure to score against.
p150a.ref: Six warm folds across two processes, cold fold discarded in each: 37.001, 37.151, 37.668, 37.756, 37.862, 38.158 s, median 37.712, the two arms 37.756 and 37.668 (0.23 % apart). Alternated in one benchlock hold with a same-day OpenFold3 control on the same card: three arms reading 38.500 / 37.035 / 37.154 s, pooled median 37.154 s, so OpenBind-0 folds this fixture 1.5 % slower than OpenFold3 measured beside it. The control's own arms are the honest caveat on this cell: arms 2 and 3 agree to 0.32 % but arm 1, folded first while the box was still busy, reads 3.96 % slower than arm 2, and the published OpenFold3 cell of 38.254 s sits 2.96 % above the same-day pooled control. So compare this number to the control beside it rather than to the row above. All six folds agree on CIF sha ('f5ae1145ccb4842b',) and plDDT 0.559887; digests compare between arms of one host and card and nowhere else. tt-quietbox2, one Blackhole AI Processor of a p300c board, physical card 3, 11x10 Tensix grid, ttnn 0.68.0, git 283b64f3, shipped defaults at one diffusion sample.

h200.detail: OpenBind-0 runs upstream v0.5.0 and the OpenFold3 columns were measured against preview2, a release that keeps the fused attention-pair-bias route v0.5.0 drops; the reference measures the two 1.07x apart on device at this size, so OpenFold3's denominators are not this model's. Its own H200 reference was run on a single-sequence fixture and does not belong in this table. Nobody has rented a box for it on this one.

row.name: PXDesign
row.target: beta-galactosidase (1DP0 chain A) cropped to 512 residues around one fixed epitope, 80-residue binder, 592 tokens
row.note: This row is what `tt-bio design --model pxdesign` returns: the PXDesign-d generator, which writes a binder backbone with no sequence. The four-model filtering pipeline upstream runs after it (ProteinMPNN, AF2-IG and a Protenix filter) is not on the CLI. Both columns time the same three steps, featurise, generate and write the CIF, with the checkpoint load outside the cell on both sides. The 1.326x lead this row shows is host and dispatch, not compute. The reference's own instrumentation says so: over the generator's 28.583 s of device stage the H200 holds 69.2 % mean utilisation at 326.8 W of a 700 W part, so 19.788 s of it is device-busy and 8.794 s is bubble inside its own 400-step loop, and a further 2.161 s of the cell is host featurisation and CIF writing where the Tenstorrent cell pays 0.069 s for the same two steps. Against that 19.788 s the Tenstorrent cell's 23.171 s of non-host time is 1.171x slower, and the comparison is generous to us in one direction only: the H200's figure is discounted for its own idleness and ours is not, so 1.171x is an upper bound on the H200's device advantage. Read this row as a win on dispatch and featurisation, not as a Blackhole AI Processor out-computing an H200. Asking for eight backbones from one trajectory instead of one is worth 1.98x per design to the H200 and takes it from 70.9 % to 98.9 % utilisation, measured at this row's own 512 residues because the term is 5.25x at 116 and 1.43x at 768 and does not interpolate. The eight are independent designs, no two within 17.68 A CA RMSD, at no cost in AF2-IG quality. Nothing equivalent has been measured on Tenstorrent, so this row stays off the per-server and per-dollar charts until it has. The LacZ crop is a cost fixture: the reference records its designs as well-folded and non-binding, because the epitope is an arbitrary exposed loop and one design per target is far below what a real campaign runs. Right fixture for seconds, wrong one for quality.

p150a.ref: Eight warm designs across two independent processes, four each, cold design dropped in both: 22.890, 22.902, 22.903, 22.918, 23.563, 23.565, 23.842, 23.912 s, pooled median 23.240. The two legs median 23.242 and 23.233, 0.04 % apart, against a within-leg spread of 4.1 % and 4.3 %. 592 tokens, 512 target residues, 80-residue binder, n_step 400 and one design per call asserted from what the call received: n_sample is backbones out of ONE trajectory, so four designs means four calls, not --num_designs 4. Every design finite, and each written CIF parses to 80 residues, 321 atoms and one chain, because write_design_cifs writes the binder alone and the C-terminal OXT is the 321st atom. The four seeds each reproduce their coordinate digest in both processes, cold round included. fp32 diffusion, the shipped default via PROTENIX_DIFFUSION_FP32_DEVICE, against the reference's bf16, an asymmetry that runs against this cell. tt-quietbox2, one Blackhole AI Processor of a p300c board, physical card 3, 11x10 Tensix grid, ttnn 0.68.0, git 283b64f3, under a benchlock hold.

split.ref: Featurisation and the CIF write, timed inside the same process as the generate step. The three leaves partition the per-design wall by construction and the recorded residual is under 0.02 s. Featurisation is 0.069 s because conditional_templ is int64 distogram bin indices at 2.8 MB, not an (NT, NT, c_z) embedding: the 65-wide table is applied on the card inside the model.

best_batch.ref: No batch term measured on Tenstorrent for this model. n_sample is backbones out of one trajectory here as on the GPU, so the lever exists in principle; the pass that measured the GPU term held no card. Until it is run this column is batch 1 and the row cannot go on the per-server or per-dollar charts, because that would give one side a lever and not the other, which is the whole reason RFdiffusion3 is off them.

h200.ref: Cells laczc512_exte_n1_msa, laczc512_prev_n1 and laczc512_prev_n1_msa of perf/pxdesign/gpu_reference.json, the generator stage's own wall clock (gen_feat + gen_device + gen_write): 30.4243 / 30.8129 / 30.9251 s, median 30.8129, spread 1.63 %. One warm rep per cell after a discarded cold rep. The three run the same target CIF, the same hotspots and the same 80-residue binder, differing only in the eval preset and in whether the target YAML carries an msa key, which read_design_yaml documents as parsed and ignored because PXDesign-d has no trunk. A fourth cell reads 31.8163 s with LAYERNORM_TYPE=fast_layernorm exported, which the shipped CLI never sets, and is excluded; that flag is inert end to end, the two cells' whole-pipeline seconds agreeing to 0.08 %, so the 2.9 % gap in the generator stage is that stage's own run-to-run noise at one warm rep. Excluding it raises the Tenstorrent ratio, since the median of all four would be 30.8690 s. N_sample 1, n_step 400, bf16, tf32 on, checkpoint load outside the cell, torch 2.13.0+cu130 on a rented single-H200 node.

split.ref: gen_feat 2.083 s and gen_write 0.078 s of laczc512_exte_n1_msa, the same two host steps the Tenstorrent cell carries inside its own number.

best_batch.ref: Measured on a rented H200 on the reference's own pin, three reps per arm with rep 0 dropped cold, both arms in one session on one exclusive card (no other compute app on any rep). N_sample 1 generator wall 32.4746 s warm median, N_sample 8 123.2831 s, so 15.4104 s per design and 2.1073x on that box. This cell carries the more conservative 15.5962 s instead: the box's host featurisation ran 4.60 s against the published cell's 2.1528 s, which inflates a wall amortisation, so only the device ratio is transferred (N=8 device 118.5885 s against N=1 27.7841 s, 4.2682x for eight samples) onto the published cell's own host timings. Its device half reproduces the published cell to 2.8 %, 27.7841 s against 28.5825 s. Batching is what fills this card: mean utilisation over the generator's own window goes 70.9 % at 329.0 W to 98.9 % at 423.8 W of a 700 W part. Amortisation is strongly size-dependent and cannot be interpolated: 5.254x at 116 residues, 1.434x at 768. The eight are independent designs, not one design eight times, which is the condition for this number to be a throughput gain at all: 28 pairs of the eight 80-residue binder backbones, zero identical, pairwise CA RMSD 17.68 / 54.64 / 73.68 A min/median/max, reproduced identically across all three reps. Quality is not degraded against the N=1 arm either, on every metric AF2-IG reports: median af2_plddt 0.935 against 0.93, monomer pLDDT 0.955 against 0.955, monomer pTM 0.813 against 0.789, ipAE 27.23 against 27.31, binder self-consistency RMSD 0.50 A against 0.77. AF2-IG binding success is 0 of 24 and 0 of 3, i.e. false on both arms, because the fixture is a cost fixture with an arbitrary epitope, so that flag cannot discriminate here and is not read as if it could. Artifacts perf/pxdesign/n8_512/.

b200.detail: The PXDesign GPU reference was a single rented H200 session. Nothing about the model prevents a B200 run; nobody has paid for one.

row.name: Nesso-1
row.target: CDK2 ladder 512 aa plus one ligand, 532 tokens, no MSA

p150a.parity: worst scalar 3.43x the reference spread, inside a 5.0x floor
p150a.ref: 8.341 s warm forward plus 13.710 s featurisation, both from one process on qb1 card 2 with the box quiet, 2 reps and the warm one taken: perf/nesso1/size_ladder.json rung aa512, arm bf16. ttnn 0.68.0.

split.ref: Featurisation is RDKit conformer embedding plus an ESM-2 650M pass on host, timed in its own right in the same process as the forward. It is the cold pass, so summing it against a warm forward is an upper bound on the whole prediction: a screen that reuses the cached embedding pays less. The device half, 8.341 s, is exact.

h200.ref: One rented H200 NVL at a 600 W power limit, driver 595.58.03 -- this is the one GPU cell on the page measured on a different H200 part, where every other h200 cell is the 700 W SXM part in a DGX H200. Cell ladder_aa512_cueq of perf/nesso1/gpu_reference.json: invocation wall 3.9403 s over 4 reps, of which the cuda-synchronised Lightning predict step is 1.0509 s. torch 2.13.0+cu130, cuEquivariance kernels on and engaged on 100 % of the triangle calls. Model load is outside the cell on both sides.

split.ref: host_s of the same cell: preprocessing 1.959 s and the ESM-2 pass 1.020 s dominate it. Same regions as the Tenstorrent cell, which is why the host halves are comparable and the whole-to-whole reading is the honest one.

b200.detail: The Nesso-1 GPU reference was a single rented H200 session. Nothing about the model prevents a B200 run; nobody has paid for one.

a100.ref: Machine 144644, A100 SXM4 80 GB at a 400 W limit, driver 580.159.03, 30.72 effective vCPU from the cgroup quota. state/perfpage_a100/nesso1_ladder_aa512_cueq_a100.json, the same invocation-wall region the h200 cell holds: warm median 7.9019 s of reps 7.9019 / 7.8397 / 7.9114, spread 0.91 %, cold rep 12.0353 s discarded. Of that, the Lightning predict step is 1.85434 s and the device forward 1.8523 s. cuEquivariance engaged on 100 % of the triangle calls (2432 of 2432 on both the cueq and the callsite counter). Peak allocated VRAM 1792.9 MiB. Affinity scalar 1.248613 against the H200 NVL arm's 1.234643, both ok. The stack is byte-matched to that H200 NVL reference: torch 2.11.0+cu128, cuequivariance-torch 0.11.1 with -ops-torch-cu12 0.11.1, lightning 2.6.5, transformers 5.15.1, rdkit 2026.3.5, nesso 1.0.0, and the same 30.72 effective vCPU on both boxes.

split.ref: predict_step is 1.854 s of the 7.9019 s cell and the rest is host: the RDKit conformer preprocess and the ESM-2 pass, timed in the same process. Same regions as the Tenstorrent and H200 cells, so the three host halves are comparable.
